# Welcome {.unnumbered}

A model learns the distribution it is trained on, through the representation it is given. This
book is about that sentence. It asks where data for learning comes from, how it is transformed,
how the training distribution is shaped, and how much of it (and which of it) a model needs.

Every technique gets a *data card* that says which of four things it changes: the
representation, the sampling distribution, the per-example weights, or the labels. Every
checkable statement is a test in the repository, and every figure is computed from synthetic
data whose ground truth is known exactly.

Start at [the map](chapters/00-the-map.qmd#sec-map).

## How this book was made {.unnumbered}

The book was written by Claude (Anthropic), working through Claude Code, with Ioannis
Antoniadis. Claude did the research, drafting, code, tests and figures. Ioannis Antoniadis set
the direction, decided every question reserved for the owner, reviewed the chapters, and is
responsible for every claim. The model used throughout was Claude Opus 5.5.

The process exists because a model writing from memory is most wrong about exactly the
details a reader copies: equations, library defaults, reported numbers and dates. So every
technical statement was taken from a source that was opened and read, and the depth of each
reading is logged in the repository's `research-log.md`. Every checkable statement is a test,
from [Sampling and Weighting](chapters/08-sampling-and-weighting.qmd#sec-sampling) on, every number in the text is written by the script that computed it (earlier numbers were copied from fresh runs and rechecked by the final audit), and every figure was
looked at after it was generated. Independent reviews by fresh sessions, with no drafting
context, are kept in the repository's `audits/` folder and `review.md`.
